requiredFindings.title: Remove the unconditional anonymous-RSS upper-bound claim
requiredFindings.problem: memory.peak is the peak of charges to the measured cgroup subtree. Anonymous pages can remain charged to an outside cgroup while mapped by a workload process, so the asserted never-smaller guarantee is false. Shared pages also do not reproduce a sum of per-process RSS.
requiredFindings.impact: The separately labelled charge metric is acceptable for exploration, but its stated conservative relationship to workload resident memory can mislead budget interpretation.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Remove the unconditional inequality and unqualified RSS-conservatism claim. Define completeness for the kernel-reported charged-memory quantity, state external/inherited/shared charge ownership limits, and keep RSS qualification/baseline equivalence explicitly with D13. Do not describe a charged-memory budget result as proving the existing RSS budget.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Pin per-run charge intervals and runner accounting in the harness
nonBlockingObservations.observation: The successor harness should define fresh-cgroup or supported same-FD-reset intervals, collection failure/incomplete handling, containment and controller availability, and record cache/charge ownership, swap and effective limits. A lifetime peak reused across warmups/runs is not seven per-run samples. These are mechanism details rather than a second objection to selecting the charge metric.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Label wait4 information as reported resource usage
nonBlockingObservations.observation: Linux wait4 ru_maxrss can include maxima inherited from reaped descendants; it is not necessarily the selected process's independent own maximum. Keeping it informational is sound. Use a reported-wait4 label and retain the no-budget-input rule.

requestAssessment.citedLines: AQ:268-272, QG:263-270, LQM:923-925 and AQC:142-146 support the stated product/preview distinctions and statistic requirements.
requestAssessment.successorRouting: Adequate for the proposed exploratory choice: PLAN:335 routes qualification to D13; PLAN:428-442 forbids G13 input/promotion until the reviewed successor, and PLAN:544 names the DR-G13 owners. Existing AQ/QG/LQM accepted requirements are not amended by this review.
requestAssessment.method: Kernel-reported hierarchical charge high-water is a sound distinct exploratory quantity without process-event attribution. The unconditional RSS upper-bound is not sound; C2-AQ-R5-01 is the required correction.
requestAssessment.baseline: A charged-memory result does not establish compatibility with an RSS baseline. D13 must decide qualification semantics; mechanism/cache/charge boundaries must be comparable for new exploratory baselines.
requestAssessment.scope: Exactly three diff hunks: title, r5 changes paragraph and the peak-memory replacement. No statistics, threshold, workload, successor-owner or other substantive edit outside that amendment.
requestAssessment.acceptanceNote: The retained PLAN-r4.md comparison has no separate acceptance-note deletion hunk; current r5 is a proposal and this review does not carry r4 acceptance forward.

verification.method: Read-only diff and line checks against accepted authorities plus static primary Linux documentation/source checks.
